commands: rm -rf build && mkdir -p build/deps build/classes build/mod

(cd build/classes && find . -name '*.class' | sed 's|^\./||' | sort) | while read -r rel; do outer="${rel%%\$*}"; outer="${outer%.class}"; for m in spring-web spring-core spring-jcl; do if [[ -f "src/$m/src/main/java/$outer.java" ]]; then mkdir -p "build/mod/$m/$(dirname "$rel")"; cp "build/classes/$rel" "build/mod/$m/$rel"; break; fi; done; done

for m in spring-web spring-core spring-jcl; do (cd build/mod/$m && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | sort > ../../$m.files && jar --create --file ../../$m-5.3.38-SNAPSHOT.jar --no-manifest @../../$m.files); done
notes: As the evaluation's jars were made: javac --release 17 -proc:none of spring-web's org/springframework/http/HttpHeaders.java (the class under test) plus all of spring-jcl, with -sourcepath over the spring-web, spring-core and spring-jcl main sources, so javac compiles exactly the classes HttpHeaders reaches; compile-only class path jsr305 3.0.2, log4j-api 2.21.0 and slf4j-api 1.7.36 (Maven Central; JSR-305 meta-annotations and the optional logging APIs spring-jcl's LogAdapter checks for; not on the run-time class path). The class files are split into one jar per source module (jar --create --no-manifest); spring-jcl also gets its META-INF/services/org.apache.commons.logging.LogFactory. The project's Gradle build is not used. Version 5.3.38-SNAPSHOT is the commit's gradle.properties version (the parent of the fix). Fixed version: spring-core, spring-jcl and spring-web 5.3.38, the first patched release.
